learn.pageTitle: Riichi Mahjong Fu for the Wait: Kanchan, Penchan, Tanki
learn.pageDescription: How the wait adds fu in riichi mahjong: two-sided (ryanmen), closed (kanchan), edge (penchan), single-tile (tanki) and pair (shanpon) waits, with tile images.
learn.whatIsMachi: What are fu for the wait?
learn.whatIsMachiBody: Depending on the shape of your [[tenpai|ready hand]], fu may be added when you [[hora|win]]. The narrower the [[machi|wait]], the more likely it is to add fu.
learn.twoFuBody: Three waits add 2 fu: the [[kanchan|closed wait]] (kanchan), the [[penchan|edge wait]] (penchan) and the [[tanki|single-tile wait]] (tanki). They accept few tiles and are weak waits. An edge wait comes in two forms: 1-2 waiting on 3, and 8-9 waiting on 7.
learn.zeroFuBody: The [[ryanmen|two-sided wait]] (ryanmen) and the [[shanpon|pair wait]] (shanpon) are 0 fu. They accept many tiles and are considered strong waits.
learn.nobetanNote: * A nobetan (a run of four such as 2-3-4-5, waiting on 2 or 5) counts as a single-tile wait and adds 2 fu.
